wedge: party size + route preset + editable car efficiency/fuel + official toll lookup + representative parking + editable rail/bus fare + station/terminal access + destination local-mobility allowance => show the household-specific crossover point where driving becomes cheaper or more useful than KTX/bus; the product sells the decision boundary, not exact live routing
last_material_result: One bounded data-maintenance feasibility round survived. A low-maintenance 3-archetype schema is feasible without paid/live routing APIs if presets are explicitly approximate and every volatile monetary field is user-editable. Korea Expressway Corporation exposes public toll lookup and route information; municipal sources expose representative parking inventories/rates (Busan publishes public-parking grade rates from KRW100-700 per 10 minutes and daily caps from KRW2,400-21,000; Gangneung publishes a public off-street parking inventory including Gangneung Station and major tourist areas). Busan also publishes local bus fares, giving a sourceable destination-mobility baseline. Rail discounts and ticket prices are the main volatile layer, so the MVP should not promise live ticket pricing: store an example/base fare with updated-at/source metadata and require or encourage user override. Minimal schema for Seoul-Busan city trip, Seoul-Gangneung local-mobility trip and Seoul-Jeonju day trip: origin/destination label, road-distance estimate, official toll lookup link/value, fuel efficiency, fuel price, parking daily allowance, public-transport base fare per person, origin first-mile allowance, destination local-mobility allowance, party size, optional time-value toggle, source URLs and updated-at. This keeps maintenance bounded to occasional preset review rather than continuous API synchronization.
economics: KRW0 validation spend. MVP can be static GitHub Pages with client-side calculation and no paid API/backend. Monetization thesis: route-specific SEO pages -> ads plus parking/rental-car/travel affiliate and portfolio cross-promotion. A small asset contributing KRW10k-50k/month remains plausible only if long-tail organic acquisition works; monetization is unproven and should be tested via smoke-test traffic before any paid infrastructure.
next_checkpoint: FOUNDER GATE: approve or reject a zero-spend smoke-test BUILD. If approved, build one reusable static calculator plus exactly 3 preset landing states (Seoul-Busan city trip, Seoul-Gangneung local-mobility trip, Seoul-Jeonju day trip), with all volatile costs editable, source/update labels, no live routing API, and anonymous view/result-use intent counters only. Then launch to GitHub Pages and validate organic/distribution demand before expanding routes.
recommendation: BUILD a zero-spend static smoke-test MVP. The maintenance-risk condition passed because exact live fares/routing are not required for the decision-boundary wedge; volatile values remain editable and presets carry source/update metadata. Do not add live map APIs, scraping, accounts, subscriptions or paid infrastructure.
